scope_note: SG-MA-PHARMACIST-ADMINISTRATION after a further correction following the V10P audit. The Manager of Record stays the filer under 247 CMR 20.02 and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D, and the circular's sentence that the administering pharmacist or intern "remains responsible for reporting the event to the Board ... in accordance with Board regulations" is kept as Department guidance; the section now says the texts leave that person's remaining responsibility open and gives the safe course (the event reaches the Manager of Record at once and the required report is made in time), instead of settling it as a flat negative. Changed: orientation[8], worked_examples[4], common_traps[21] and [22], retrieval_prompts[24] and [25], role_duties[9] and exceptions[8]. Events outside 247 CMR 20.02(2) and s. 39D(c) are now "not required to be reported" under those texts, with a note that the circular is broader. orientation[10], worked_examples[1].steps[3], ma_vs_federal[0] and quick_review[26] now describe 21 CFR 1306.07(a) without an unqualified "only" and add (b) and (c), neither of which provides for prescribing. No rule changed; the grounding rests on MA-ADMIN-ADVERSE-EVENT-REPORTING, MA-SERIOUS-EVENT-REPORTERS-AND-TRIGGERS and FED-NARCOTIC-MAINTENANCE-DETOX-ROUTES. Scope gate: the same 13 actionable signals as the previous freeze are declined (collaborative drug therapy management prescribing, MA-PHARMACIST-PRESCRIBER-ID, and contraception and expedited partner therapy records). All six practice links stay.

prior_audit_reference.note: V10P rated the superseded hash MINOR_EDIT at Medium and drove these corrections. It does not bind the hash frozen here and is excluded from the auditor package.
